notes.title: ﻿Server Regions Reduction
notes.content:
2024-07-24 Update: Thanks for all your considered feedback. Based on this we will be reducing to 3, not 2 server regions.

We have decided to reduce server regions. The following regions will be ramped down as of August 1st 2024:

Australia (OCS - Sydney)
Western USA (NAW - North California)

The servers in Japan (AST - Tokyo), Eastern USA (NAE - North Virginia) and Europe (EUC - Frankfurt) will continue to operate as normal, with no plans for shutting them down.

This will concentrate players on the remaining servers. We're hopeful this will make finding matches easier, especially for new players.

If you have any questions, please reach out via our contact form:
https://www.digitalconfectioners.com/contact/

notes.title: Retiring Community Treasures & Treasure Marketability Changes
notes.content:
As the application of gambling regulations to video games changes, and potential new legislation is introduced in jurisdictions around the world, we want to ensure that Depth is available for as many of our players as possible. As outlined in Depth's 2018 Roadmap we will be retiring the sale and trade of all treasures in one week. While free reward treasures will remain in Depth, to comply with all international laws treasures from any source will no longer be sold by us, nor marketable on the Steam Marketplace. Note that this change applies only to the treasures themselves, any skins which are unboxed will remain marketable for the foreseeable future. At this time, we have no plans to make skins from the Community Treasures available on the Depth Item Store, however this may be something we may look to exploring in the future to continue to support our content creators. In recent months about 12% of Depth's revenue has come from treasure sales, so while this is some money it is not a large enough amount that it will impact our update schedule or content patch sizes.

Edit: Added FAQ
Which treasures exactly will not be tradeable/marketable?
All Treasures - this includes the Community Treasures, Event Treasures, Quest Treasures, etc.

Will my skins remain tradeable/marketable?
Yes, all skins will remain tradeable/marketable. This includes skins obtained from treasures both past/future.

Is Depth going Free-to-Play?
We currently have no plans of going Free-to-Play. (This question seemed to come up a lot below.)

Are you turning off the Steam Marketplace?
No, we have no plans on turning off the Steam Marketplace. Only the treasures themselves will no longer be marketable. All the skins will remain on the market, and remain marketable.

notes.content:
Depth: Ghouls & Goblins
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/ad6338f9e92104de35458805af41d66bf8a6aeac.png
Dr. Larson and his team at Impact Labs have been hard at work, and are ready to unleash their fearsome Goblin shark! Genetically modified to thrive in shallower waters and given greater strength, this Goblin poses a real threat and is sure to strike fear in the hearts of divers. Celebrations for the end of the Terror Nights are underway once again, so stay alert for when ghouls and goblins attack!

Introducing the Goblin!
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/13b857cd97386a0ffe1aea94811de49ef5256a02.jpg
The Goblin is best known for its terrifying extendable jaw packed full of needle-like teeth, and its distinct surfboard shaped nose. Although sluggish in nature, the Goblin makes up for this in combat with its intimidating appearance known to incite panic in divers.

Ability: Terrify
Strikes fear in the divers, causing them to hallucinate another goblin shark.

1: Hallucination Health: 1
2: Hallucination Health: 60
3: Hallucination Health: 120

Ghouls & Goblins Event
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/eddd575dd0d2e68034458aa6d6c24f6c8c37eb45.jpg
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/d208ec34f0d6b17a67227974bf601ed0071ea713.png
The Ghouls & Goblins event is packed full of rewards to earn and things to do! Sink your teeth into a new event treasure unleashing 15 new skins into Depth! Earn event treasures as rewards by playing Depth, or purchase them from the Depth item store.
Ghouls & Goblins brings a new leveling commemorative coin, however this time with a twist! Select levels of Commemorative Coin will reward you with a gravestone which drops upon your death in-game. Gravestones will only be usable during the event.
This event will also feature a skin tournament, Tools vs Teeth! Featuring sharks and diver gear, earn points for your favorite in each match-up by playing games of Depth. The winner of the skin tournament will have a Hadal rarity skin created for it, and runner-up one of Abyssal rarity!

Improving the New Player Experience
With this update we've focused on improving the new player experience in three key ways: improving matchmaking, introducing recommended builds, and reworking how players unlock gameplay content.

To address matchmaking for new players, we've made adjustments to improve the matching algorithm to reduce how often experienced and new players are matched with one another. Wait times may be slightly longer on average with this change, however we feel this better match quality will make Depth a more enjoyable experience for new and experienced players alike.

Recommended Builds are a new way for players to learn to play new species of sharks more effectively. All players will be able to switch to the full evolution view whenever they would like.

We believe that unlocks should be both rewarding and an enjoyable way to explore what Depth has to offer. With the new unlock system, players will complete small challenges to unlock Sharks and Diver Gear. Shark Evolutions and Weapon Upgrades are now all unlocked by default, and all veteran players will get to keep any content they had previously unlocked.

Front End Notifications - Stay Informed!
At the main menu, we've added a new area for displaying messages for improved communication about what is happening with Depth, such as update progress or server maintenance periods.

notes.title: Depth: Shark Fight - Goblin vs Oceanic Whitetip
notes.content:
Depth: Shark Fight - Goblin vs Oceanic Whitetip

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/d37af32a4e7ee5f7fe5fe3a666e0320c12886e34.png

Impact Labs is a group of rogue scientists led by former Aquatekk Industries researcher Dr. Larson. The lab is well known for taking on any project - given the right price. Recently they've picked up a contract of questionable ethics, that aims to identify a species of shark to transform into the ultimate man eater. Two sharks have been identified with the best potential for the project; the Goblin and Oceanic Whitetip. Sides have formed in the lab, and its up to you to help prove which species is the best! Will you fight on the side of the Goblin Shark, the living fossil with a menacing extendable jaw? Or will you fight on the side of the Oceanic Whitetip Shark, a shark known for its dangerous and aggressive behavior toward shipwrecked crews? Choose which side you fight for in the main menu and as you complete matchmade games of Depth your score will earn points for your selected side! The side with the most votes at the end of the event will be chosen as the next shark species added to Depth!

Shark Fight - Treasure

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/46b7fca975d9d56901407d07729d3360d0cb9765.jpg

Depth's first event treasure has come ashore! Complete games of Depth during the Shark Fight event to earn Shark Fight Event Treasures! Featuring a variety of new designs for sharks and divers alike, you'll want to be sure to keep an eye out for creations from Impact Labs such as Stitches the Bull Shark, and their heavily modified Harpoon! The Shark Fight Event Treasure will also be available for purchase on the Depth Item Store for the duration of Shark Fight. Event treasures and items gained from Shark Fight will be tradeable and marketable at the conclusion of the event.

Shark Fight - Commemorative Coin

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/fcc7d34927279590ddc731969fd6b419842e5535.png

To commemorate Shark Fight we've released another leveling event commemorative coin! Similar to previous events you level your coin by earning score in completed matchmade games of Depth, but only before Shark Fight ends!

Item Crafting - A new way to recycle!

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/0bcfaca5e85212ef2827fabb8822fbcddfcd103b.png

Impact Labs has setup an interesting way to recycle the old into the new! Their lab is available for use in crafting new items now in the Store's Crafting area in the main menu, and will even be sticking around after Shark Fight ends. So if at any time you find yourself with items that you don't need anymore, give crafting a whirl and who knows what will come out!

Introducing the Social Bar

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/6740526/94e0a4b35d0a59c7eda3d28072b2e53eb9e4ebff.png

With Shark Fight we've change how lobbies and the friends panel are presented while still delivering the same functionality as before by condensing them into a new area called the Social Bar. This has opened valuable space along the right side of the main menu which we will continue to tweak in the future.

Changelog for patch available here.

Depth: Dragon Dance

Learn the basics with an all-new tutorial, create your own weapon skins, play in Turkish and more!

 Added Steam Workshop support for diver gear!

 Controller default bind overhaul.

notes.title: Depth: Sharks with Frickin' Laser Beams
notes.content:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=656932393

In our quest for realism and accuracy, we often turn to the experts among our community for small tweaks that could improve the immersion in Depth. We have noted community disappointment at the lack of "frickin laser beams", and now intend to fix this grievous oversight.

Frickin Laser Beams

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=656933938

From watching historic media channels, we have discovered that sharks may have once been ranged predators, both killing and cooking their prey at a distance.

Changelog:
This includes the major changes since the last update (minor bugfixes and changes are not included) 

Mechanics


Replaced Dart with Laser attack for all sharks
Sea Mines now smarter and chase after sharks
P.A.T.: Can now correctly target a shark in Line of Sight (LOS), if another closer shark is out of LOS.


Balance


Bull Shark no longer gains rage in Hide and Seek.
Updated spawn protection for both Sharks and Divers.
P.A.T.: Base detection range reduced to 1000 from 2500.
P.A.T.: Now has unlimited targeting range on tagged Sharks.


Maps


Fixed godspots on: Station, Temple, Fractured (B&G, HS), Olmec, Devil's Head, Antiguo, Hillside, Wreck (Thanks Sinopia!)
Antiguo: Fixed some clipping issues. Fixed some badly placed rubble in the ravine (only visual). Smoothed two walls with blocking volumes, one at safe 2, one at Safe 3.
Devil's Head: Smoothed edges in many locations where horizontal tunnels transition to vertical shafts.
Fractured: Removed hole in ship near Safe 2, which only allowed Divers to pass through.
Galleon: Filled in holes in the ship near Safe's 2 and 4, which was allowing divers to shoot through some corners. Fixed a couple spots where you could slide in between some breakable grates on ceiling of safe 3.
Olmec:  Adjusted collision for shelves near Safe 4 to be more accurate relative to visible mesh. Updated the window breakable to have a collision that fits to the bounds of the window.
Stash: Repositioned overturned door a bit to remove a Godspot from underneath. Fixed Safe 3 doorway due to the terrain misaligned with the bottom of the frame.
Station: Moved Ammo/Medkit spot upwards at Safe 3 so it no longer spawns under the landscape.


Content


Fixed issue with caustics which was making maps appear darker than intended



Sound


Corrected Shelly pain noises which had been set incorrectly.


Other


Treasure pieces now begin falling if they are on a breakable which is destroyed
Minor adjustment to readying times for consumables to hopefully fix issues with them visually remaining in-hand after placing.

New Map: Temple
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531676607
Built to worship the Aztec goddess of oceans, Chalchiuhtlicue, this now time-worn temple crumbled into the sea during the late-1800's. The temple hadn't been fully explored before it disappeared, with recent expeditions heading under to both preserve and excavate the site.

Serrated Teeth - Shred Puny Divers
Tearing flesh to shreds, this abso-bloody-lutely vicious evolution leaves bitten divers to slowly bleed until they reach a Medkit... or death.

StubbsCare - Free Medkits and Diver Health Bars
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=531677839
There's good news and bad news. The bad news is, while you were napping a bunch of other salvage groups have found out about our target locales. The good news is, so far their expeditions have failed, and they've even left a few extra supplies on the bottom of the sea. Stubbs says there's a good number of Medkits down there now, in between the corpses.

notes.content:
Fresh Blood is Depth's latest free update adding two new playable divers Finn & Shelly, a Blood & Gold variant of Station, scopes, new diver upgrades, new evolutions and more!

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274290

New Divers: Shelly & Finn

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274564

Shelly: Lead scientist for the Specimen Program at the Aquatics Research Lab, Shelly specializes in cybernetic organisms and was responsible for the creation of Specimen 8. After Specimen 8's escape to open water, Shelly was tasked with recovery of the beast due to her intimate knowledge of its systems and capabilities.

Finn: An astute surgeon and well read marine biologist, Finn oversees all medical operations and upgrades within the Specimen Program. With considerable experience handling the beasts, Finn was the first choice to join Shelly in the recovery of Specimen 8 after its escape from the Aquatics Research Lab.

New Map: Station

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=510274710

Satiated by the taste of any blood, evolutions that trigger on diver kills now also trigger after seal kills.

ON SALE FOR 20% OFF UNTIL SEPTEMBER 14TH 2015

notes.title: Hide and Seek Update!
notes.content:
Click here to go to the update website!

New Game Mode: Hide & Seek

With this update we're adding a new game mode, Hide and Seek. One player starts as a shark, and must hunt down the divers. When a diver is killed they join the shark side, and killing all divers secures a win for the sharks. But beware - diver players can defend themselves with their Bang Stick!

Hide and Seek is launching with five maps - including versions of Fractured and Galleon, as well as new maps Wreck and Station. We've also included a new community made Hide and Seek map from Gameo, called Mausoleum. You'll find Hide and Seek under the Private Match section of the Play menus.

New Map: Stash

Just off the coast of Cuba lies an abandoned and forgotten submarine base. With its roots tied to the cold war era and hints pointing to a nuclear involvement this relic is said to hold stashes of cached weapons that could bring a pretty price to the right buyers.

New S.T.E.V.E. Weapon Skin Pack

http://store.steampowered.com/app/384240/

Alongside this update we're releasing the new S.T.E.V.E. Weapon Skin Pack, on sale for 20% off until July 12th, 2015! Fight with the style of the divers' robotic overlord S.T.E.V.E! The S.T.E.V.E. Weapon Skin pack adds new finishes for the SPP-1 Pistol, ADS Rifle, Sea Mine, and LJ-10 Volleyjet.

Note: Skins will not be available for use in-game until patch releases

Changelog:
This includes the major changes since the last update (minor bugfixes and changes are not included) 

Mechanics

Fixed bug where the sensor was awarding points to the diver when 'detecting' a stealthed Tiger shark.


UI

Bot Match is now renamed to Private Match.
Fixed bug where the in game scoreboard was not correctly handling dead players.
Improved UI visuals when switching between diver gear skins and diver gear categories.


Maps

Added new map Stash.
Quarry's safes now award $1000 from $500.
Cove: First Safes up from $1000 to $1300
Cove: Last Safes down from $1000 to $700
Fractured: First Safes up from $1000 to $1200
Fractured: Last Safes down from $1000 to $800
Olmec: First Safes up from $1000 to $1100
Olmec: Last Safes down from $1000 to $900
Added Community label when loading Community made maps.
Added low quality shader mode for Hillside to improve performance for lower end computers.


Content

Added Hide and Seek game mode.
Added S.T.E.V.E. diver weapon skin DLC.
Added Gold skins for Net Gun, Sensor and Spear Pistol which are awarded when you have a Depth Badge Level 1 from crafting cards.
Fixed bug where diver gear skins would sometimes not show correctly.
Optimized all of the diver gear materials to reduce their shader instruction count.


Sound

Updated to WWise SDK version 2014.1.1 which fixes some issues with some audio cards.


Steam

Players set to max level no longer receive Level 100 Crown.


Other

Removed game dependency on .NET, also removed the .NET preinstaller.
Added 64-bit version of Depth.
Performed package maintenance to reduce the size of Depth overall.
Depth SDK is now the same content and tools that we use for development.
Dedicated servers can now specify more than six players and the game correctly selected the correct number of sharks and divers.

notes.title: Whiplash Update!
notes.content:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458153725
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zOuf19QLSDU
Whiplash is Depth's latest free update adding the all new Thresher shark, a community map 'Quarry' by Gameo, aim-down-sights, custom crosshairs, new weapon modifiers, and more!

Introducing The Thresher - The Sting Of A Whip
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458158376
The Thresher doesn't look notably dangerous with its unassuming jaws, however its true weapon is a long, blade-like tail capable of lacerating and disorienting multiple prey at once.

Introducing Quarry - A New Community Made Map
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458157965
This long deserted limestone quarry has become an underwater battleground strewn with naval sea mines and full off colossal crystals.

This map was made in DepthED by Gameo, a member of the Depth community.

Reef Stalker - Tiger Skin
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458154718
The only proof of this beast's existence is the trail of dismembered bodies it leaves in its wake. The few who claim to have seen it speak of a monstrous tiger shark that strikes without warning and then disappears into the darkness. Locals have named it the "Reef Stalker" after its favored hunting grounds.

Sawtooth - Mako Skin
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458155116
The only thing uglier than this Mako's face, is its temperament. Born with a genetic abnormality that caused its teeth to form into jagged 'saws', it is more than capable of tearing prey limb from limb, and has been responsible for a rash of attacks on wreck divers in recent months.

Rebuilt Main Menu And Spawn/HUD Improvements
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458159797
We've re-built the main menu for Depth, updating it with our fresh new UI style which we debuted with the Ship Wrecked update for in-game menus. This new style improves performance with reduced memory usage, while providing crisp clear visuals on 4k (and above) resolutions!

Lock On To Sharks With Aim Down Sights
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458159465
As a diver you can now use Aim Down Sights functionality with (by default) the Right Mouse Button. We've even added an optional spherical aiming system to Aim Down Sights, so you can shoot 'over vertical', for tracking pesky sharks swimming directly above or below you.

Crosshairs Just The Way You Want Them
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458157518
Unhappy with the default Depth crosshair? Then make your own with our new custom crosshair system. There's options for the size, style, and color of various parts of the crosshair - and we've included a bunch of templates from the community for you to try out.

Play Your Way With Expanded Weapon Modifiers
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=458163816
We've added a whole host of new weapon modifiers for divers to customize their loadout.

Click Here for More Information.

notes.title: Prepare to be Ship Wrecked!
notes.content:
This weekend you'll be getting wrecked in all new ways with a whole raft of new content. You can check out the update website for Ship Wrecked, or browse the major features we'll be shipping below:

Introducing the Hammerhead - It's Hammer Time

The Great Hammerhead fights tooth and nail as he thrashes and bashes prey to a crimson pulp. Modest jaws are made up for by pinning prey behind the cephalofoil and crushing them to smithereens. Crushing is a brand-new mechanic unique to the Hammerhead, direct impacts into any solid object will cause prey in his jaws to take damage proportional to the speed and angle of the hit. The Hammerhead is a force to be reckoned with and may just put the final nail in your coffin.

Introducing Shark Abilities - Shark species' special skills

Every shark in Depth has been given a new and unique active ability. Unlike evolutions, which are entirely 'passive', these abilities are player activated (E by default), so you can use them whenever you feel the time is right! Shark abilities are available and equipped at the start of every game. Along with a base level, Shark Abilities can be upgraded a further two times (with the same Evolution Points you know and love) giving added effects and bonuses. Without further ado, let's dive into the details!

New Map: Galleon

El Magdalena was a Spanish War Galleon which met its demise after crossing paths with an English Man-Of-War off the coast of Cuba in 1643. Immense chunks strewn across a bouldered sea floor are decorated with loose cannons, cracked masts, and booty galore. S.T.E.V.E. and the divers are geared up to descend to the depths of this wreck in hopes of discovering the lost treasures of Diego Sanchez that lay within.

Introducing the LJ-10 Volleyjet - Lock, stock, and 10 barrels

Built from experimental technology, the LJ-10 Volleyjet simultaneously fires a ring of ten, 9.4mm Lancejets which spread as they travel. While inaccurate at great ranges, the LJ-10's steel tipped Lancejets will tear through any shark in close-quarters combat.

Introducing the Medkit - Enough drugs to knock out a whale

Who knows where Captain Stubbs dredged this stuff up but boy does it work. Got a headache? Use the Medkit. Bleeding a bit? Use the Medkit. Get your limbs mangled by a ravaging shark but are somehow still alive? Use the Medkit. It's a wonder why they didn't bring this down sooner considering how effective it is!

Introducing the Welder - Turn up the heat

Putting the hype in hyperbaric, this handy welding torch does it all from performing repairs on S.T.E.V.E. to cutting enraged sharks off your limbs. Stubbs will appreciate you keeping our favorite robot in such great shape! Be sure to give it a shot errrr... a weld!

The Armament Rearrangment (UI/HUD Upgrades)

With a brand new visual style, Depth's in-game menus have been expanded and improved in what they do. Weapons have been broken down into categories and rearranged, allowing us to release an advanced weapon upgrade system. Ammo upgrades have been distributed among every weapon where appropriate, allowing you to tag and tranquilize like never before. For example: With the new upgrade system you could add tagging rounds to a P11, or tranquilizing rounds to your SPP-1! Along with these changes, you'll find that the in-game HUD and scoreboards have been updated to reflect the new visual style.

Ship Wrecked Achievements

Get lost in 6 brand new achievements!

Define your style with Depth Skins!

Alongside the Ship Wrecked update is the release of the Legendary Hammerhead and Corsair weapons skins - define your style with these jawesome skins!

notes.title: Progress Update! - Content Patch 2
notes.content:
It's been a while since we showed any progress, and we feel bad for leaving you in the dark like that. Tons of stuff is going on behind the scenes right now, and we figured we owe you an explanation as to why things are taking so long!

So, for starters, we wound up overshooting the goals we outlined in our Q1 2015 Roadmap. When we started working on that content, we quickly realized that it could tie in to some new gameplay opportunities that would require more work, but could open up some seriously cool new mechanics in Depth. Well, we got a little ahead of ourselves and probably bit off more than we could chew. But we're finally getting close to finishing now, so the time is right to shed some light on what we have been up to 

STEVE Damage & Repair

STEVE is a pretty crucial part of game, for both teams. He sets the pace of the divers progress, and contributes significantly to their chances of winning or losing the match. The problem is that while sharks can damage and disable STEVE quite easily, destroying him is very difficult. This was a deliberate choice on our part because we ran out of time to fully flesh out STEVE's health and damage system and felt that making him super tanky would get around the problem. And it does... kind of. But we really wished that we could come up with more interesting mechanics that would make divers truly care about protecting STEVE from sharks, and would open up new tactics for sharks that involve trying to take STEVE out of the game completely.

To this end, we have re-balanced the way sharks deal damage to STEVE:

STEVE no longer takes 'stacking' damage from sharks
STEVE takes a fixed damage amount based on the size of the shark hitting him. Larger sharks hit harder.
STEVE no longer regenerates health on his own.
The more damaged STEVE is, the slower he moves.
As a result of these changes, STEVE is quite a bit more vulnerable to sustained ram attacks from sharks. To counter this, we have created a new diver item that allows divers to make repairs to STEVE on the go - "The Welding Torch".  It's quite affordable, and support focused divers should be able to keep STEVE in tip top condition if they choose to purchase it.
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406877277 
Oh, and in case you were wondering - the welding torch is separate from the new diver gear we promised in the 2015 road-map. Expect more diver gear to follow!

UI Redesign

We're taking the opportunity to both refresh the look of Depth's menus, as well as expand and improve what the menus do. As an example, the diver spawn menu in Depth saw many revisions before launch, ending up with the current layout:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406888770 
This layout has some limitations:
Inefficient use of the screen space (see the top-right)
An intimidating wall of icons for buying weapons
New players don't see progression-locked weapons (so the game looks content-light)
Adding many more weapon choices will run us out of screen space

We've iterated a lot on both the visual style and the flow of the menus, winding up with something more like this:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406889392The whole screen space is used
Weapons are broken up by category
We're able to show progression-locked weapons to new players

But beyond fixing the limitations of the old menu, the new menus give us some cool new features, some of which become clear in the new weapon details screen:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406889422  
Weapon Upgrades! You're going to have a lot more options for how to tweak your loadout with the new content patch. And the number of weapons and upgrades the new menus will comfortably support is huge. On top of that, there's more information on weapons shown, and choosing skins for weapons is better supported. For example: With the new menu system you could add tagging rounds to a P11, or Tranquilizing rounds to your SPP1!

Leaderboards

An updated version of Depth's leaderboards will be rolling out with the update to address the issue of scores being reset undesirably, along with some new changes :

All Leaderboards will be seeded with the scores from all previous months. Almost all reset scores will be included thanks to regular backups
All Leaderboards will be made lifetime, and no longer reset monthly
All Leaderboards will be made Crown Eligible, if you are in the Top 10 on any leaderboard you will be seen with a dazzling crown in-game

AI Updates
Another area that wasn't on the roadmap but we felt strongly needed some love was our bot AI. AI for both sharks and divers have received updates for interacting with more elements of gameplay including:

Shark AI responding to Shark Shields and no longer attacking hidden targets without first getting close to them
Shark AI will attack STEVE when opportunity arises
Shark AI will go for seals when low on HP
Diver AI will place both Shark Shields and Sonar Buoys

Shark Species Abilities

When we started working on the new shark evolutions we promised in the roadmap, we felt like it would be a lot more interesting if instead of just adding a handful of generic evolutions, we instead added some that were unique to each of the shark species. We quickly realized that this wasn't going to work in the context of the current evolution economy. How could players 'buy' something that we wanted them to have from the beginning? Should we just make it super expensive? What about really cheap? After a great deal of back and forth we settled on the idea of adding 'abilities' instead of 'evolutions'.

http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406873872

Each shark species (Tiger, Mako, Great White) will now have its own built-in ability that does not need to be purchased to use. However, this ability can be improved by spending evolution points on it. We are still working out the finer details but as an example, we present to you the Tiger's ability which we call 'Adaptive Hide'. It applies a temporary camouflage effect to the tiger's skin that allows it to slip in and out of combat without being detected by sonar buoys or flares. (it also makes you somewhat harder to spot by divers, too of course!) Unlike evolutions, which are largely 'passive', these abilities are player activated, so you can use them whenever you feel the time is right!

We are very excited about these new abilities as we think they will add a whole new level of 'Depth' (OK, that one's getting old now) to the shark game.


New Map!

And If none of that convinced you that we've been working our butts off on this update, then I hope these shots of our new map will!
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406891930  
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=406891872  
We will be revealing more details about the map and the rest of the content in the upcoming update in the next few weeks, scout's honor!

Finally, we would like to thank all of you for playing Depth and having faith in our promise to provide continued support for the game.  Our goal is to do more than just add new content.  We would also like to refine what content and mechanics are there, and improve every aspect of the game.  Your feedback is a huge part of this, so please let us know what you think of our changes and what you would like to see tweaked or improved in the future! ːgreatwhiteː

notes.title: The Big Catch Update
notes.content:
The Big Catch is a brand new free update for Depth bringing: the Megalodon Hunt game mode, two new playable sharks, The Tiger and Mako, a new map and more. Reel it in today!

New Game Mode: Megalodon Hunt
Megalodon Hunt is an all-new game mode for Depth. Five divers face off against the greatest and most ferocious shark conceivable - the powerful Megalodon. Megalodon Hunt is void of S.T.E.V.E. and instead of focusing on room-to-room combat concentrates on map-wide chaos. Divers scramble for treasure as the Megalodon puts up a relentless fight, however as divers get stronger the tables turn and the hunter becomes hunted. 

New Map: Devil's Head
Devil's Head – A flourishing gold mine turned abandoned shark haven. With three floors of winding tunnels and large excavated rooms, Devil's Head focuses on indoor combat within its flooded halls. Vertical exploration is a huge part of Devil's Head - as S.T.E.V.E. and the divers wind deeper in the mine, the sharks come and go as they please using deserted elevator shafts and busting through aged wooden structures. Divers and Sharks alike will be sure to find themselves adapting and working together within this sunken quarry! 

New Shark: Mako
The Mako may be the smallest of the trio, but don't let that trick you; he's fast as hell and twice as mean. With a sleek but fragile frame the Mako is built for speed and agility. With great finesse and carefully aimed attacks the Mako excels in one-on-one combat. Using his smaller frame to slip in and out of rooms, divers are sure to keep on their toes as he whisks their allies into the dark. 

New Shark: Tiger
The Tiger is a real man eater, and his striped hide makes him hard to spot. With a solid build and powerful muscles, the Tiger is adaptable to a wide variety of strategies ranging from hit-and-run to all out aggression. Putting his bulky framework to use means the Tiger is more than capable of taking a few bullets before making a lively escape. 

Rebalanced Great White
The Great White is as large as he is dangerous. With the introduction of shark classes we've reworked the Great White into a close quarters powerhouse taking full advantage of his enormous size. Being both slow moving and hard hitting the Great White will continue his onslaught as bullets and spears sail his way. 

New Gear: Shark Shield
Sharks are darn good at sensing but why let them! Utilizing a wide range of electro-magnetic frequencies the Shark Shield will disrupt the senses of any shark as long as it's powered on and make any diver inside its effective area undetectable. However with portability comes fragility, any shark that gives it a good ram should send it flying away in pieces. 

Depth Ed
We'll be reeling in DepthED with the Big Catch Update for those of you looking to dive deeper into Depth. This is a full suite of editing tools that allows players to create their own maps and mods for the game. If you'd like to know more and talk about the Depth Editor join us on our Steam Forums – Mapping and Modding subforum. We can't wait to sink our teeth into what you guys release. 

New Achievements
We've added nine new achievements to the Blood & Gold game mode and four new achievements for the Megalodon Hunt game mode.

notes.title: Depth: Controllers and Performance
notes.content:
This patch focuses on controller support and performance, along with a few fixes that we thought couldn't wait for the big content patch.

Full Controller Support

It's here! Full controller support - including XBox 360, XBox One and PlayStation 4 controllers. This includes vibration support for XBox 360 and XBox One controllers, as well as full re-binding and configuration for all supported controllers.

We still recommend a good gaming mouse and keyboard, but for those that prefer their trusty controller, the depths can now feel at home.



Performance

The complex dynamic lighting in Depth continues to be the biggest challenge for performance. We've done a lot of profiling and analysis, hunting down key performance hurdles, particularly for shark players. We found several areas that we were able to optimize with more aggressive culling, LOD'ing and optimization techniques.

The gains are quite large, and should see shark players getting in many cases double the framerate of previous versions. Diver players will see much smaller improvements.

For those who are curious, here's a video peek into a frame of Depth.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aO6P7Wd9pqI

Changelog:
This includes the major changes since the last update (minor bugfixes and changes are not included) 

Balance


Divers suiciding inside a sharks jaws now just count as a shark kill
Divers suiciding very near to a shark will still be a suicide - but give the nearby shark an evolution point


UI


Rank Up leaderboards messages improved to show only when important


Maps


Cove: Slowed down the first safe unlocking, sped up the second safe unlocking
Cove: Added some more treasure near the first safe


Sound


Added new sounds for plane impacts and destruction in Cove
Heartbeat logic tweaked to be more granular (and therefore useful) to divers


Steam


Rank Up achievement is now given for being in the top-100 of any leaderboard


Other


A couple of crash issues solved
Server ping improvements
Bangstick net code rebuilt (now much more fair)
XBox 360 controller support
XBox One controller support
Playstation 4 controller support
Skylight performance enhanced
Directional shark lights halved in cost
LOD system added for culling and optimizing diver flashlights

notes.title: Depth Beta Update: Final Beta!
notes.content:
A big thank-you to everybody who has played Depth during the beta period. We've received a lot of useful feedback, and have been able to make a number of improvements based on it. Our focus in this patch has been performance and polish.

Performance

We've made numerous optimizations to Depth since the last update. Some small, some quite large. Their impact on your experience will vary a lot, but we're confident that everybody should get at least a 10% boost in framerate. Some hardware configurations will get much larger (even as much as 100%) boosts.

Map Balance

We've been watching carefully how the maps have been playing out in beta, and have made a lot of small tweaks based on both metrics that we record, and feedback from the community.

Some breakables have been added to areas in some maps to slow things down, giving divers a bit more time to set up around safes. We've also done a lot of work on treasure in the maps, with some maps seeing re-distribution to smooth out bumps in diver economy, and all maps getting tweaks to stop unreachable treasure.

notes.title: Depth Beta Update: Sounds, Languages, and Lobbies!
notes.content:
It's been a while - and this is a big patch. A few major features have been in the works for months, and have finally arrived!

Rebuilt Sounds and New Sound Engine

Our sound guys have been working on this for months, and it's finally here! Everything about sounds has been completely re-built - a new more powerful sound engine is in use, and the sounds themselves have had a lot of work done.

This means improved occlusion, positioning and levels. You can now hear bullets whizzing by your head, and gunshots can be heard at long range (even if they're quiet). With HDR sound support, explosions don't distort, and loud sounds cause tinnitus effects when they're too close.

Many of the source sounds have been re-done as well, with guns like the ADS sounding far more solid. In short, Depth just Sounds Better (tm)!

Translations

We've also just finished up the first wave of translations for Depth. This sees Depth being available in English, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Russian, Polish and Brazilian Portuguese.

While patch notes are only available in English, the Steam store page, Steam achievements, the game itself, and our website are now all available in all 8 languages. We're excited to be making Depth a whole lot more accessible for so many players.

Better Lobbies

We've built a public lobbies system where you can advertise your lobby to the world through an in-game lobby browser. This provides an alternative method to matchmaking for players to group up before starting games of Depth. You can filter public lobbies by region, and see descriptions and details for each lobby.

We've also worked hard on making our core lobby functionality smoother and more robust than it's ever been before.
